name: Data.Pair.isIntegralMeasure_intAlgPart
summary: Points det((1, g_x)/(1, g_y)) over pairs of the class representatives g = u·twistLift(A), coefficients the class sums of Gram forms of the integral point kernels; the norm of the lift expands into this sum.

steps.claim: Let g(u, A) = u·twistLift(A); take the index set of pairs (x, y), the points u_{(x,y)} = det((1, g_y)/(1, g_x)) and coefficients built from class sums of Gram forms of the point kernels: they are integral at l prime to Q, since the class counts divide the order of the chosen group (`Data.card_classAut_dvd_chosenGroupOrder`), the scaled point kernels are integral (`Data.Pair.weylGauge_pointKernel_le_one`, `gramForm_mem_embValRing`) and the inverse power of the norm of Q is an l-unit; it remains to expand intAlgPart.
steps.lean:
lemma isIntegralMeasure_intAlgPart : ϑ.IsIntegralMeasure (intAlgPart H) := let g (a : StdClasses
    (n := Unit) D.chosenLevel × TwistGL _ Unit) := a.1.out * (D.levelPlaces ϑ).twistLift a.2
  ⟨_ × _, _, fun x ↦ G.det (s := 1) ((1, g x.2) / (1, g x.1)), _, fun x l _ hl j ↦
    (@embValRing _ _ ⟨j⟩).1.mul_mem (smul_classSum_mem _ (D.card_classAut_dvd_chosenGroupOrder (K :=
    (lValueData H ϑ).auxPair.levelGroup) (H.1.trans_le D.nat_le_of_hasLogBound) levelOf_le_Kf)
    (gramForm_mem_embValRing _ (weylGauge_pointKernel_le_one H (ϑ.pow 0) (g x.2) _ hl) <|
    weylGauge_pointKernel_le_one H _ (g x.1) · hl))
    (by simp [hl.norm_natCast_eq_one, -Nat.cast_prod] : ‖j (ϑ.levelNorm ^ (card n - 1))⁻¹‖ ≤ 1), by
  rintro ⟨⟩ rfl
  rw [sum_prod_type]; simp [intAlgPart, ← coe_algebraMap, ← inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, inner,
    LevelForm.innerAt_eq_stdClassSum, mul_sum, sum_div, classSum_sum, ← coe_inv_eq_conj,
    ← mul_classSum, trivialLift_apply, TameChar.pow, kernelValue, pairWeil_apply,
    rankTwist, ↓map_div]
  congr with; congr with; ring!⟩

steps.claim: Let ϑ′ have the modulus of ϑ.

Expand intAlgPart(H, ϑ′): the squared norm is the inner product of the lift with itself, a class sum over U(2z) (`LevelPlaces.LevelForm.innerAt_eq_stdClassSum`) of products of the expansions of `Data.Pair.trivialLift_apply`; the kernel values of the twist ϑ′ are those of ϑ times ϑ′ at the points (`Data.TameChar.pow`, the Weil action of the points).
steps.lean:
rw [sum_prod_type]; simp [intAlgPart, ← coe_algebraMap, ← inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, inner,
    LevelForm.innerAt_eq_stdClassSum, mul_sum, sum_div, classSum_sum, ← coe_inv_eq_conj,
    ← mul_classSum, trivialLift_apply, TameChar.pow, kernelValue, pairWeil_apply,
    rankTwist, ↓map_div]

steps.claim: The two expansions agree term by term (a ring identity).
